evidence.red_check: Attempt 1 - full pre-fix swap - was abandoned. Checking out config.py, run_pipeline.py and services/slack.py wholesale from 6b53085a3^ made the pipeline abort before the Slack step (deploy_succeeded=False, no Slack step recorded at all): unrelated later commit 61bc2e4c6 rewrote run_pipeline against a new models.ImageRef / aws.deploy_ecs signature, so the pre-fix module no longer loads against today's siblings. Restored immediately and switched to a surgical reverse-patch: recorded sha256 of the three shipped files, then `git revert -n 56f625609` plus `git apply -3` of the reversed 6b53085a3 src diff. Both applied cleanly, giving exactly the pre-OR-2691 logic on top of current code (config.py:98 SLACK_CHANNEL = "#product-dev", AWS_PROD url guidedor-prod.guidedclinical.com, no SLACK_ANNOUNCED_BY_CI guard, old message text, no ok:false check). Re-ran the identical driver: all four checks went red at once. Dev posted channel='#product-dev' text='<@U123> deployed GuidedOR to guidedor-dev.guidedclinical.com (AWS Dev)' - wrong channel, no app link. Prod posted 'deployed GuidedOR to guidedor-prod.guidedclinical.com (AWS Prod)' - the stale host. The SLACK_ANNOUNCED_BY_CI=true scenario posted anyway (1 call, status SUCCESS) - the double-post. The ok:false scenario reported StepStatus.SUCCESS with no error logged - the silent failure. Also ran the shipped test suite against the reverted src: 7 failed, 33 passed, including test_ci_deploys_stay_quiet_because_the_workflow_already_announced and test_notify_raises_when_slack_rejects_the_post_with_http_200 (40/40 green before the revert). Then reverted: `git reset && git checkout -- .`, `git status --porcelain` empty, `shasum -a 256 -c shipped.sha256` reported OK for all three files, and re-ran the driver to confirm the positive case is back (channel C076GD57VV1, app link present, CI scenario SKIPPED with 0 calls, ok:false scenario FAILED).

caveats: This ticket changes deploy tooling and CI, not the application - nothing was or could be exercised against the running app at localhost:62582, and the red_check_signature will not appear in the app container log the gate greps; it is a literal line from the captured deploy-pipeline run output instead.

The runtime exercise stubbed the network boundary: slack.com was intercepted with respx and AWS/ECS/git/maven were stubbed, so the assertion is on the exact HTTP request the shipped code emits rather than on a real post landing in Slack. Real posts landing correctly is covered separately by the production Slack history.

GitHub Actions expressions in .github/workflows/deploy.yml were not executed locally (no act, no actionlint available); the CI half rests on production evidence - real #notifications-deploys messages and the deployment API environment_url.

The prod branch of the APP_HOST ternary in deploy.yml has never run: the GitHub deployment API has no aws-prod deployments, so prod is deployed via local bin/deploy. The equivalent constant on that path (config.AWS_PROD.url) is confirmed correct by the 2026-08-21 prod Slack message.

The 'cancelled' and 'failed' Slack steps in deploy.yml were verified only for the cancelled case (a real cancelled dev deploy on 2026-08-24 posted the app link); no failed CI deploy was available in the window read.
continue-on-error on the four Slack steps was not exercised - it needs a genuine Slack API failure inside a CI run.

automation.assessment: Unit coverage is already strong and demonstrably load-bearing: tools/deploy/tests/test_slack.py and test_run_pipeline.py hold 40 tests, 7 of which go red against the reverted source, and they cover the channel default being an ID, the SLACK_DEPLOY_CHANNEL override, the ok:false rejection, the message text for AWS and OpenShift, the SLACK_ANNOUNCED_BY_CI skip, the empty-token skip, and the non-fatal outage path. Nothing needs to be duplicated there. Two real gaps remain. First, no test asserts the composed wiring end to end - every pipeline test stubs slack.notify, and every test_slack.py test calls notify() with a literal message, so no test would catch a correct message being sent to the wrong channel or a correct channel receiving a message assembled wrongly. Second, .github/workflows/deploy.yml has no coverage at all, and it is where the ticket's user-visible requirement (the app link) actually lives for CI deploys.

jira_comment:
Validated deploy-ready.

This was validated against the merged change on main (PR 4241 and PR 4266), using the production Slack workspace plus a runtime exercise of the real deploy pipeline code with the Slack API intercepted at the HTTP boundary.

Positive: #notifications-deploys now carries the app link. CI deploys post "deployed orci:202608241823-e7eeafd to dev (guidedor-dev.guidedclinical.com) - View Details", and local bin/deploy posts "deployed orci:0.1.92 to AWS Prod (guidedor.guidedclinical.com)", which also confirms the stale guidedor-prod host was fixed. Running the real PipelineRunner emitted channel C076GD57VV1 with the linked host for both dev and prod. The GitHub deployment API returns environment_url https://guidedor-dev.guidedclinical.com, so the shared APP_HOST value resolves in the environment URL as well.

Negative: no deploy notice has reached #product-dev since the merge. The last one posted at 2026-08-03 11:22 EDT, twelve minutes before PR 4241 merged, and the channel has carried none in the three weeks since despite roughly twenty deploys. A CI deploy also does not double-post: with the announced-by-CI flag set the pipeline made zero Slack calls and reported the step as skipped while the deploy still succeeded.

Red check: the pre-OR-2691 logic was reverse-patched into the three changed source files and the same run repeated. All four checks went red together - the message went to #product-dev with no app link, prod showed the stale guidedor-prod host, the CI deploy posted a second time, and a Slack rejection returned as HTTP 200 with ok:false was reported as success. The shipped test suite also went from 40 passing to 7 failing. Everything was then restored, checksums re-verified, and the positive case re-run green.

Caveats: this is deploy tooling and CI, so nothing was exercised against a running application. Slack and AWS were intercepted rather than called for real. The GitHub Actions expressions were not executed locally; that half rests on the production Slack history and the deployment API. The prod branch of the workflow host expression has never run, since prod is deployed locally rather than through the workflow.

Automation: unit coverage is already strong and load-bearing, so nothing needs duplicating. Two gaps are worth closing - an end-to-end assertion on the actual channel and text the pipeline emits (today every test stubs one side or the other), and any coverage at all for the deploy workflow, via actionlint plus a check that the rendered notification text names the right host for dev, stage and prod.
